title: Product Window
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the maximum product of any contiguous subarray of size `k`.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4], k = 2
Output: 12 (Subarray [3, 4] has product 12)

Example 2:
Input: nums = [-2, -3, 4, -1, -2], k = 2
Output: 6 (Subarray [-2, -3] has product 6)

hints.1: Consider a sliding window of fixed length k. Can you compute the product of the first window and slide across?
hints.2: When sliding, you can multiply by the incoming element and divide by the outgoing element, or track rolling products safely when zeros are present.
hints.3: Watch out for zero values and negative numbers that might flip signs.

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
statement: Given a 1-indexed array of integers numbers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific target number.

hints.1: Since the array is already sorted, can two pointers starting at both ends help?
hints.2: If sum < target, increment left pointer; if sum > target, decrement right pointer.

title: Valid Parentheses Evaluator
statement: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

hints.1: Use a stack to push opening brackets.
hints.2: When encountering a closing bracket, check if it matches the top of the stack.
hints.3: Ensure the stack is empty at the end.
